chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi al-Ward, who said:
I said to Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, or Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, “May Allah set you aright,”
A man was attacked by an insane man with a sword, and the insane man struck him a blow. Then the man took the sword from the insane man and struck him and killed him.

He عليه السلام said: “I hold that he is not to be killed for him, nor is he to be made liable for his blood-money. Rather, his blood-money is upon the Imam, and his blood is not to be left uncompensated.”

key_terms.بِالسَّيْفِ: with a sword, indicating armed assault
key_terms.دِيَتَهُ: his blood-money, the financial compensation due for a killing
key_terms.عَلَى الْإِمَامِ: upon the Imam, meaning the authority bears the compensation
key_terms.فَقَتَلَهُ: so he killed him, describing the fatal act in self-defense
key_terms.مَجْنُونٌ: an insane person lacking legal accountability
key_terms.يُطَلُّ دَمُهُ: his blood is left uncompensated or in vain

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone kills an insane attacker while defending himself?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a person who kills an insane attacker in the course of defending himself. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the defender is neither subject to retaliation nor personally liable for the diyah; rather, the diyah of the insane person is borne by the Imam, so that the blood is not left without compensation.
